newsitem.title: CANADA: Westcoast lifts brief plant force majeure.
newsitem.headline: Westcoast lifts brief plant force majeure.

text.p: Westcoast Energy Inc declared a force majeure on Wednesday at its McMahon natural gas plant in northeast British Columbia but lifted it soon after when operational problems cleared up, Westcoast Field Services division president Irv Koop said.

"We made a business decision about an hour ago when it looked like we would have to change the business flow tomorrow based on reduced throughputs at the McMahon plant where we are having some constraints at our sulfur plant," Koop said in a phone interview.
"But we are as we speak running full volumes through McMahon...there will be no change to the business flows for tomorrow."

He said the company had yet to determine what caused Wednesday's problems at the 700 million cubic feet per day plant, which has been plagued with a series of operational upsets over the past several months.
"But for some reason it's cleared up and we are not now restricted by the sulphur plant," Koop said.
McMahon, the company's largest processing facility, was also shut down for a few hours on Tuesday after mechanical problems occurred in its control system.
